title: Paella
subtitle: with soy curls and spring vegetables
menu_blurb: Saffron rice with smoky paprika soy curls, roasted asparagus and artichokes, and colorful peppers, all cooked together in one beautiful pan.
intro: A beautiful, colorful, and very flavorful dish that will exceed all expectations.
origin: Paella comes from the Valencia region of eastern Spain, from the rural lands around the Albufera lagoon. Its modern form emerged in the mid 19th century as a humble meal for farm laborers, but its roots are much older. It blends two cultural influences: the Moors, who brought rice cultivation and saffron to the region around the 10th century (the Spanish arroz comes from the Arabic al-ruzz), and the Romans, whose flat cooking dish, the patella, is believed to have given the paella pan its name.

mise_en_place.label: Soak
mise_en_place.task: Saffron in hot water, and soy curls in warm water

mise_en_place.label: Chop
mise_en_place.task: Onion, peppers, artichokes, garlic, and asparagus

mise_en_place.label: Tools
mise_en_place.task: A paella pan and a baking sheet

items.name: Large red peppers (or 10 small colorful peppers)

steps.title: Prepare
instructions: Steep 2 tsp of saffron in 2 cups of hot water.
Soak the soy curls in warm water, enough to cover, for about 20 minutes.

steps.title: Roast the asparagus and artichokes
instructions: Trim the asparagus stems. Spray with olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and roast at 400°F.
Slice the artichokes lengthwise and roast them the same way.
Remove both from the oven once they get a little crispy, and cut the asparagus into 1-inch pieces.

steps.title: Brown the soy curls
instructions: Squeeze all of the water out of the soy curls.
Cook them in the paella pan with olive oil and half the garlic, 1 tsp of each paprika, 1 tsp of salt, and a little pepper. Stir until browned, adding oil as needed.
Taste and add more paprika, salt, and thyme if you like.
Push the soy curls to one side and cook the onion on the other side until soft.

steps.title: Build the paella
instructions: Add the tomatoes and mix well.
Add the rice and mix well.
Arrange the sliced peppers on top in a pretty pattern.
Add the rest of the spices: thyme, paprikas, salt, and pepper.
Pour in the vegetable broth and saffron water. The pan should be fully covered; add water if needed.

steps.title: Simmer
instructions: About halfway through, add the asparagus and artichokes.
Simmer on low until all the liquid is absorbed. Try not to stir until it is almost gone; if it starts sticking, stir a little.
Taste and add seasoning, or more water if the rice isn’t fully cooked.

tips.label: Flavor boost
tips.tip: Add more paprika, thyme, and salt as needed.

tips.label: Substitution
tips.tip: Add spinach, carrots, beans, or other hearty vegetables you like.

tips.label: Meal prep hack
tips.tip: Keeps well in the fridge for several days, and it freezes well.

notebook.question: What are soy curls, and are they good for you?
answer: Yes! Soy curls are made from non-GMO whole soybeans, without chemical pesticides, preservatives, or additives. They are also a great source of protein, fiber, iron, and potassium.

notebook.question: What’s the difference between soy curls and tofu?
answer: Tofu is minimally processed but not a whole food. It provides high-quality protein, healthy fats, and often added calcium. Soy curls are closer to a whole food than most processed soy products, retaining the fiber and protein of whole soybeans, though some nutrients are lost in processing.
